summary: Taiko Yamasaki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Koyasan University under Bokushō Kanayama and held posts at Koyasan University and Shuchiin University.

Tainori Tanigawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D. by 1994), later serving at Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 1980-1988) and professor (attested 2005).
Taion Satomi focused on Buddhist studies, graduating from Rissho University in 1933. He later served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1972).

Tairyo Makita studied at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University (~1934-1939). In Buddhist studies and sinology, he served as professor at Kyoto University (~1957-1976), taught at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and became president of Saitama Institute of Technology (attested 2001).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 1996).

Taishu Tagami, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University (~1954-1958) and the University of Tokyo (~1958-1963). In 1990, he was attested as a professor at Komazawa University and concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute.
Taishun Mibu specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After completing his studies at Taisho University in 1937, he later served as director there (attested 1972).

Taitetsu Unno worked in Buddhist and religious studies after studying at UC Berkeley (~1947-1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1951-1968). He subsequently served as professor at Smith College (~1971-2007).

Taixu studied under Jichan (~1904-1907) in Buddhist studies. He founded the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1918; leader in 1927), Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1922), Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1930-1931), and Tianning Buddhist College (1931).
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen.
Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki studied at Ryukoku University (~1948-1957), later serving there as professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (1970) and president (1989-1995). A Buddhist studies scholar, he was also chairman of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (~2007-2014).

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Matsumoto Fukashi High School, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1900-1903), Waseda University, and the University of Paris (~1916-1920). He held a post at Waseda University from ~1906 to 1940.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University and Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, did postdoctoral work under Heinz Bechert, and lectured at Bukkyo University (attested 1999).
Takanobu Takahashi worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Shitennoji University and served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from ~1996 to 2017.

Takanori Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Komazawa University. He served as research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973-1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichoji (attested 2003).

Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and the history of science. He studied at Tohoku University (~1968-1977) and Brown University (~1979-1985) under David Pingree, later serving as Professor of History of Science at Doshisha University (~1989-2015).
Takao Kagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.
